title: APIs with FastAPI
summary: Nimbus's agents are only useful once other programs can call them: a website, a mobile app, a partner. **FastAPI** turns typed Python functions into an HTTP API with validation, documentation and clear errors from the same declarations. This module builds the Nimbus API: endpoints and parameters, request and response models, one error shape, dependencies, routers, settings and lifespan, middleware and CORS, and a support-reply endpoint backed by the model.
learn: Your first app: path operations, JSON, the free `/docs`, and running it with uvicorn
**Path and query parameters**: types, enums, rules, parameter models, and 422 before your code runs
**Request bodies and responses**: models in, a different model out, status codes and headers
**Errors** in one shape, **dependency injection**, **routers** and a project layout
**Settings and lifespan** (create the model once), **middleware**, **CORS** and GZip
flow:
browser / app ─→ CORS ─→ request id + timing ─→ GZip ─→ FastAPI: route → dependencies (settings, API key, audit, model)
   → validate → your function → return model (filters internals) ─→ JSON          any error → {"error": {"code", "message"}}

labs.explain:
The **Nimbus API** serves orders and the café menu with typed parameters. The lab sends the same nine requests (good ones, a missing order, wrong types, out-of-range numbers, a misspelt parameter) to it and to the **same endpoints parsed by hand**, and scores which answered correctly, which crashed, and how much bad input reached the code.

Type your own request to compare both responses side by side.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

code.why: A typed path parameter and a return model: validation in, filtering out.

notes.match: def get_order(order_id: OrderId, store: StoreDep) -> Order:
notes.text: The return type filters: customer ids never leave the service.
A misspelt parameter is an error, not silently ignored.
Rules: FastAPI answers 422 when they're broken.

code.why: The alternative: parameters read by hand.

notes.match: def get_order(order_id):  # no type: anything gets in
notes.text: No type: no validation and no documentation.

labs.explain:
POST **/support/reply** with a valid body, nested history, and five kinds of bad input (an empty message, a 'system' turn, a huge length, an unknown field, text/plain); path + query + body in one endpoint; the schema's example; and one real reply from the model.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

The reply endpoint's **return type filtering** an internal draft (system prompt, model, tokens); **201**, **204**, **exclude_none**, headers and your own **Response** objects.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

Five failures through the Nimbus API (**your own exceptions**, one handler each, **one shape**) and through FastAPI's defaults; then an **unexpected bug**: a generic 500 with a request id for the client, the details in the log.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

An **API key** dependency read from a header, an **Annotated alias**, a **sub-dependency** that runs once per request, **yield** dependencies with both cleanup scopes, an **app-wide audit**; then the Nimbus API's own key check and audit log.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

code.why: The key, checked in constant time.

labs.explain:
The Nimbus API's **files and routers**, its paths grouped by tag, one router mounted as **/v1 and /v2**, and the **create_app factory** building two differently configured apps.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

Typed **settings** from the environment, the cached get_settings(), and ten requests to an app that builds a model client **per request** against one that builds it **once in the lifespan**.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.match: app.state.chat_model = chat_model or get_chat_model(settings)  # ONE client for every request
notes.text: Created once, at start-up; closed at shutdown.

path.title: Production path: the Nimbus API
path.summary: The Nimbus API is a create_app() factory with routers per area, request and response models per direction, one error shape, dependencies for settings, the model, the store, API keys and auditing, a lifespan that builds the model client once, and middleware for request ids, timing, GZip and CORS.

steps.title: Contract
steps.explain: ReplyRequest validates what clients send (roles, a bounded history, a length range, no unknown fields); the endpoint returns ReplyPublic, so the Draft's system prompt and model never leave.
production: The OpenAPI schema at /openapi.json is the contract: generate client types from it.

steps.title: Errors
steps.explain: ApiError subclasses (NotFound, Unauthorized, ModelUnavailable, ModelError) raised anywhere; handlers for them, HTTPException, validation errors and anything unexpected, all as {"error": {"code", "message"}}.
production: Alert on internal_error: each one is a bug, logged with its request id.

steps.title: Structure
steps.explain: create_app(store, settings, chat_model): routers for orders, menu and support; the lifespan builds the model client once and closes it; dependencies read app.state, so tests pass their own settings and fakes.
production: Set NIMBUS_API_KEYS in production: with no keys configured the API is open.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.explain:
Orders, the menu, three real replies, bad bodies and a provider outage, against a naive first version and the Nimbus API.

| | right status | errors in one shape | responses leaking internals | model clients (3 replies) | reply p50 | our front end (CORS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| First version | 9/10 | 0% | 3 | 3 | 2.7 s | refused |
| **Nimbus API** | **10/10** | **100%** | **0** | **1** | **2.5 s** | **allowed** |

The first version answered errors in three shapes (`{"detail": "..."}`, a list of validation details, and a plain-text `Internal Server Error` when the provider was down), sent its internal draft (system prompt and model name) with every reply, and built a new model client per request. The Nimbus API answers every error as `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`, turns the outage into a 503 with Retry-After, and returns only the answer and its length.
production: Module 3 turns these requests into pytest tests that run in CI.
